claim: Selecting a subset of vision encoder layers for cross-attention with a language model reduces computational cost while maintaining strong performance on vision and vision-language tasks.
falsifier: One can train a model with different fractions of selected layers and measure computational cost (FLOPs) and task performance to validate the trade-off.

conditions: Cross-attention mechanism that bypasses LLM MLP layers for visual tokens
Pre-training and fine-tuning on vision-language datasets
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported vision encoder, LLM, layer selection strategy (25% of layers), and evaluated tasks; transfer to other selection ratios or architectures is unestablished.

title: Using only a subset for computational cost and maintained
